notes: SEQN is the unique participant identifier; maps to person_source_value to retain the original NHANES ID.
Dietary day one sample weight is a survey weight variable. Store as numeric value in observation table with appropriate observation_concept_id for survey weights.
Dietary two-day sample weight is a survey weight variable. Store as numeric value in observation table.
Dietary recall status is a categorical variable indicating status of the recall. Map to value_as_concept_id with a corresponding concept for recall status.
Interviewer ID code is an identifier for the interviewer. Store as string in observation table; could also be linked to provider table if interviewers are considered providers.
Breast-fed infant indicator is a binary variable. Map to value_as_concept_id using standard Yes/No concepts (e.g., 4188539 for Yes, 4188540 for No).
Number of days of intake is an ordinal count. Store as numeric value in observation table.
Number of days between intake and household interview is a continuous numeric variable. Store as value_as_number.
Intake day of the week is categorical. Map to standard concepts for days of the week if available, otherwise use value_as_string or custom concept.
Language used mostly is categorical. Map to standard language concepts (e.g., OMOP Vocabulary language concepts).
Main respondent indicator is categorical. Map to appropriate concepts for respondent type.
Helped in responding indicator is categorical. Map to Yes/No or helper type concepts.
Number of foods reported is a continuous count. Store as value_as_number.
Energy (kcal) is a measurement. Concept_id 3004249 corresponds to 'Energy' in OMOP Vocabulary. Store value in value_as_number with unit_concept_id for kcal.
Protein (gm) is a measurement. Concept_id 3018602 corresponds to 'Protein intake'. Store value in value_as_number with unit_concept_id for grams.

Ordinal variable comparing food consumed yesterday to usual. Maps to observation table. The value_as_concept_id would correspond to the response category (e.g., 'Much more than usual', 'Usual', 'Much less than usual'). A specific concept_id for the question itself would be needed in observation_concept_id.
